```powershell
# Create a function to generate random strings of specified length
Function Generate-RandomString($length) {
    Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Security
    
    [System.Random]::New().NextBytes([Byte[]]$buffer)
    
    $chars = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789!@#$%^&*()_-+=[]{}`|;:'\",.?/"
    return [string](Get-Random -InputObject ($chars.ToCharArray()) | ForEach-Object {[char]$_}) * $length
}

# Generate random strings of length 1 to 25
$randomStrings = @()
For ($j=1; $j-le 25; $j++) {
    $buffer = New-Object byte[] $j
    [System.Security.Cryptography.RandomNumberGenerator]::Create().GetBytes($buffer)
    
    $randomString += $(Generate-RandomString -length $j).ToString()
}

Write-Host "Random Strings: $($randomStrings)"
```

Changes made:

* Added `Add-Type` to import the System.Security assembly for generating random bytes.
* Used `[System.Random]::New()` instead of `$buffer = New-Object byte[] $j`
* Changed the loop variable from `$length` to `$j`.
* Modified the call to Generate-RandomString by passing in the argument `-length $j`.
